sections.h2: How is property tax split up in Genesee County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Genesee County property tax runs through three layers: a city or township assessor sets each value, a city, township or village treasurer collects the current bill, and the county treasurer collects whatever is still owed after March 1. The county's equalization department sits in the middle and checks that the local assessors are working at comparable levels.

The county was created on March 28, 1835 and fully organized on April 4, 1836. It holds 33 cities, townships and villages around Flint, the county seat, across 636.94 square miles of land. The cities are Burton, Clio, Davison, Fenton (partly), Flint, Flushing, Grand Blanc, Linden, Montrose, Mount Morris and Swartz Creek. Villages include Gaines, Goodrich, Lennon, Otisville and Otter Lake. Which assessor and which treasurer you deal with depends on which of these your parcel sits in.

Flint is the exception to one county service. The equalization department maintains property description records everywhere in the county except the City of Flint, whose city assessor keeps its own.

sections.h2: Which Genesee County offices handle property tax questions?
sections.html:
Three county offices matter, and each sits in the county administration building on South Saginaw Street in Flint. The equalization page itself sends owners to the city or township for assessments and current bills, and to the county only for delinquent ones.

  • Equalization, Suite 8B: telephone (810) 257-3017. It prepares the annual equalization report and the millage reduction report. Assessment information comes from your city or township assessor, and current tax information from your local treasurer.
  • Treasurer, Suite 2A at 324 S Saginaw St: telephone (810) 257-3054, open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. It handles delinquent taxes and tax foreclosure. Partial payments are encouraged, and they can be made by mail, online or through an automated line at 1-877-805-2856. Online and phone payments carry an extra fee.
  • Clerk and Register of Deeds, Suite 1A: records deeds and mortgages. The separate register of deeds guide covers fees and transfer tax.

The county equalization page links State Tax Commission Bulletin 11 of 2025, which is the 2026 Property Tax, Collections and Equalization Calendar. It is the best single list of statewide dates for that year.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Genesee County homes?
sections.html:
Genesee County is the fifth most populous county in Michigan, with 401,093 people in the 2025 estimate, 1.3% fewer than in the April 2020 base. It is a county of 167,334 households and 185,007 housing units, and owners occupy 70.7% of homes.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $182,400 (2020-2024).
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,455 with a mortgage and $583 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $989.
  • Median household income: $62,281.
  • New building permits in 2025: 444.

Property tax rides on those home values, so the gap between Flint, where the median owner-occupied home is valued at $53,500, and the county overall matters for anyone comparing bills. The Flint River drains most of the county, and I-75, I-69, I-475 and US 23 cross its center, which makes the suburbs around Grand Blanc, Burton and Davison easy to reach from the city. Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How do assessment appeals work in Genesee County?
sections.html:
An owner challenges a value at the local board of review, which meets in March in every city and township in the county, and then may go to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Genesee County itself does not hear individual appeals.

State law has each board start on the second Monday in March, though a local governing body may move the first meeting to the Tuesday or Wednesday that follows. A board must sit at least 12 hours that week and at least three of the required hours after 6 p.m. Anyone who files a protest gets written notice of the result by the first Monday in June, along with the tribunal address and filing deadline. A nonresident owner may protest by letter.

For the tribunal, the petition deadline is May 31 of the tax year for commercial, industrial and developmental real property, and July 31 for residential and agricultural property. Residential owners must have protested to the board first. Two other boards meet in July and December, and they handle qualified errors, such as a clerical mistake or a wrong measurement, and certain exemption claims. A correction can reach back only to the current and prior year.

sections.h2: When does unpaid Genesee County property tax turn delinquent?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax turns delinquent on March 1 of the year after it was levied, and from that day the Genesee County Treasurer is the collector. The state timeline below applies to every Michigan county that serves as its own foreclosing unit, which includes Genesee.

DateWhat the county treasurer does
March 1, year oneReceives unpaid bills as delinquent, adds a 4% fee and 1% interest per month
June 1 and September 1Mails first, then second notice by first-class mail
October 1Adds a $15 fee
February 1, year twoSends certified notice to the owner and a mailing to the occupant
March 1, year twoParcel forfeits, a $175 title fee is added, redemption interest of 0.5% a month starts
March 30 and 31, year threeCourt judgment of foreclosure deadline, then last day to redeem

Source: Michigan Department of Treasury, Foreclosure Process Timelines.

After foreclosure, the county sells parcels at online auctions. The 2026 rounds were a minimum bid sale on September 3, a re-offer sale on September 25 and a no reserve sale on October 30. A Genesee County Land Bank exists to help return foreclosed property to the tax rolls.

sections.h2: Are there foreclosure surplus claims in Genesee County?
sections.html:
Yes, for people who lost property at auction between 2013 and 2020. The county treasurer's page describes its participation in a class settlement, Fox v. Saginaw County, for properties that sold for more than the taxes and expenses owed. The claims deadline was July 16, 2026 and has passed.

Foreclosures after July 18, 2020 follow a different route. An owner or lienholder files a Notice of Intention to Claim Interest in Foreclosure Sales Proceeds, Form 5743, and later a motion to claim remaining proceeds, form CC 540. Both forms appear on the treasurer's page. The State Bar of Michigan's referral line, 800-968-0738, is listed there for people who need a lawyer.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Genesee County house that owes tax?
sections.html:
Selling is allowed, and the unpaid tax, interest and fees come out of the seller's proceeds at the closing. Ask the county treasurer for a payoff to the closing date if the bill has already been returned as delinquent.

Transfer tax adds to a seller's costs. The state charges $3.75 per $500 of value and the county charges 55 cents per $500, because Genesee has fewer than two million residents. On a $180,000 sale, close to the county's median home value, that is 360 units of $500, so $1,350 to the state and $198 to the county, a total of $1,548. The seller is liable, and the county treasurer receives payment within 15 days of delivery of the deed. Foreclosure transfers, deeds to a child or grandchild and land contracts that keep title with the seller are exempt.

A seller who is behind on tax, or whose house needs work, can sell as-is to a cash buyer, with the payoff handled at closing in a single step.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Genesee County delinquent property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Genesee County Treasurer, 324 S Saginaw St Ste 2A in Flint, by mail, online or by phone. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and online and phone payments have an extra fee.

faqs.q: Does the county set my property's value?
faqs.a: No, your city or township assessor sets it. The county equalization department checks that local assessments are comparable across the county and prepares the millage reduction report.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Genesee County assessment to the Tax Tribunal?
faqs.a: Yes, after a protest to the local board of review for residential property. The tribunal petition for residential property is due July 31 of the tax year, and May 31 for commercial and industrial property.

faqs.q: How long before Genesee County can foreclose on unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Foreclosure takes about three years from the first March 1 delinquency. The parcel forfeits on the second March 1, and the court judgment comes by March 30 of the third year, with March 31 as the last day to redeem.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax in Genesee County?
faqs.a: The combined rate is $4.30 per $500 of value, made up of $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county. The seller owes it, and it is paid to the county treasurer within 15 days of the deed.
